title: The media server's binary: media.toml, the UDP serving loop and the signalling intake seam
spec: docs/CALLS.md 'The shape' and 'Admission'. `crewcraft-media <media.toml>`. config::parse reads [media] in the strict TOML subset (crewcraft-strict-toml, at most 16 KiB): server-name (a lowercase host name), listen (IP:port), public-address (optional; a specific address and port; without it the bound address is the ICE candidate, so listen must then be a specific address), chat-server-key (a plain file name next to media.toml) and max-call-size (optional, 1 to MAX_CALL_SIZE). config::load also reads the key file: a regular file, owner-only on Unix like the server's other keys, 64 hexadecimal characters and at most one line ending. serve::bind binds the socket and makes the MediaServer (set_max_call_size). serve::run drives it from the socket: requests from an intake::Intake (Join with a reply channel, DropPerson, EndCall), datagrams in, MediaServer::poll for str0m's timeouts (waiting 1 to 20 ms), datagrams out; when the stop flag is set it closes every session (MediaServer::close_all), sends the goodbyes and returns. intake::channel gives an in-process Handle (join waits for the answer, JoinError::Stopped once the loop is gone) and the ChannelIntake the loop drains; the chat server's control connection implements Intake later, and the binary uses NoIntake until then. main stops on Ctrl+C and SIGTERM (ctrlc), exits 2 on a usage error and 1 on bad settings. Test: on loopback UDP, two str0m clients join through the intake and A1's frames reach A2 byte for byte; stopping closes both sessions (each client sees Closed), the loop returns Ok and a later join is Stopped; the settings and key are refused when wrong (unknown key, no usable candidate, call size out of range, a path for the key file, a bad server name, a bad key, a key file others can read); the binary exits 2 without arguments and 1 naming the bad key.
